name: preterm_30wk
description: Literature reference values for a preterm neonate born at 30 weeks (~1.5 kg) at ~72 h postnatal age, stable on nasal CPAP 5 cmH2O in room air without surfactant (mild RDS), a small restrictive left-to-right PDA (~1 mm) and a small PFO, untransfused, delayed cord clamping, advancing enteral feeds + PN, caffeine, humidified incubator. Grades: A = 29-31 wk infants on day 2-4, B = wider GA band / other day / figure readout / guideline / short extrapolation, C = textbook / extrapolation / derived.
state: stable on nCPAP 5, FiO2 0.21, no surfactant, small restrictive L->R PDA, PFO, untransfused (delayed clamping), advancing feeds + PN, caffeine, incubator ~34 degC / 60 % RH

variables.label: Heart rate
variables.notes: User decision 150. Baseline HR falls with GA and rises with postnatal age (Alonzo 2018, 29-31 wk group; Eenkhoorn 2026, median 29 wk); neither gives usable numbers. Interpolated between the 28 wk anchor 155 and Groves 2011 cine 142 +/- 17 (CGA ~35, day 9, asleep).

variables.label: Systolic BP
variables.notes: Elsayed 2023 has no 30 wk row (cohort < 29 wk): day-3 centiles extrapolated linearly from 23-28 wk (median slope ~2-3 mmHg/wk). Cuff cross-checks: van Zadelhoff calculator GA 30+0 PNA 72 h 62.4 (48.1-78.1); Guan 2026 28-31 wk D3 67.

variables.label: Diastolic BP
variables.notes: Elsayed day-3 DBP rises 1 mmHg/wk from 24 (23 wk) to 29 (28 wk); extrapolated 31. Cuff 34.8 (van Zadelhoff), 36 (Guan).

variables.label: Mean arterial pressure
variables.notes: User decision: Elsayed day-3 median extrapolated to 30 wk = 42.4 (fits from 23 and 25 wk agree). Cuff reads ~4 mmHg higher, as at 28 wk: van Zadelhoff 46.1 (P2.3-P97.7 33.0-60.4), Guan 46.

variables.label: Pulse pressure
variables.notes: Derived from the extrapolated medians (28 wk 25, 25 wk 19).

variables.label: Central venous pressure
variables.notes: User decision: Choi 2015 VLBW 3.5 +/- 2.2, steady days 1-7 (as the revised 25 wk target). CPAP 5 is lower than at 25/28 wk; Inglis 2007 4.9 was mostly ventilated.

variables.label: Pulmonary artery pressure, systolic
variables.notes: Derived: RV/systemic ratio 0.50 (user decision; series 0.60 at 25 wk, 0.55 at 28 wk; Patel 2019: PAAT rises linearly with GA at birth) x SBP 58. Ratio grade B, mmHg grade C.

variables.label: Pulmonary artery pressure, mean
variables.notes: Chemla relation 0.61 x sPAP + 2; extrapolation.

variables.label: Pulmonary artery pressure, diastolic
variables.notes: Constraint: PA diastolic < aortic diastolic (~31) so the restrictive duct stays pure L->R.

variables.label: LV end-diastolic volume
variables.notes: SV 1.43 at EF ~65 %; Groves MRI: no GA effect (cohort covers CGA 30).

variables.label: LV end-systolic volume
variables.notes: EDV - SV; Groves 0.78 +/- 0.21.

variables.label: LV ejection fraction
variables.notes: Groves 69 +/- 5.7 (LLN 58), no GA effect.

variables.label: RV end-diastolic volume
variables.notes: Derived from RV SV 1.30 at EF ~50 %.

variables.label: RV end-systolic volume
variables.notes: Derived.

variables.label: RV ejection fraction
variables.notes: As at 25/28 wk (3D echo 52 %, Toyoshima).

variables.label: RV fractional area change
variables.notes: Levy 2015: 26 +/- 4 % at 23-28 wk days 1-3, 35 +/- 4 % by 32 wk PMA. Reference only.

variables.label: TAPSE
variables.notes: Koestenberger 2011 GA line 0.60 at 30 wk; Ghandi 2018 30-33 wk 0.47 +/- 0.13. Reference only.

variables.label: Left ventricular output
variables.notes: User decision: kept as at 25/28 wk. Brackets at this GA: Schwarz 2022 (median 29 wk, days 1-2) TTE 163 +/- 47; Sloot 2010 (25-31 wk, day 7) 296; Groves MRI at CGA ~30 ~260 (day 10, duct closed). LVO rises day 1 -> 2 (Cappelleri 2019, 32.7 wk).

variables.label: Right ventricular output
variables.notes: Schwarz 2022 TTE RVO 241 +/- 77 (days 1-2).

variables.label: LVO/RVO ratio
variables.notes: (Qs + PDA) / (Qs + FO), small duct.

variables.label: SVC flow
variables.notes: As at 25/28 wk. Kluckow 86 at 48 h (<30 wk); Groves MRI ~113 at CGA ~30 (day 10) = upper bracket.

variables.label: Descending aorta flow
variables.notes: Balance: LVO 215 - SVC 85 - duct ~20 - coronaries ~12 = ~100. Split: SMA 28 + coeliac 20 + kidneys ~17 + rest ~35.

variables.label: Cerebral blood flow
variables.notes: User decision (derived): tracer CBF ~20 mL/100 g/min at 28-33 wk (Greisen 1986) x brain 185 g (HC 27.5 cm, Dobbing & Sands) = 12.3 % of 1.5 kg -> 25 mL/kg/min. Same flow per gram of brain as 28 wk; the brain is a smaller share of body weight. Ultrasound cross-check Kehrer 2003 32-34 wk ~18 mL/kg/min. Brain = 29 % of SVC.

variables.label: Intestinal (SMA) flow
variables.notes: Time-averaged over 3-hourly feeds (advancing feeds ~60 mL/kg/day): postprandial peak at 30 min, near baseline by 60 min (Maruyama 2013; +83 % at peak, Martinussen 1996); CPAP blunts pre- and postprandial flow (Havranek 2007). Between-feed baseline ~25.

variables.label: Renal blood flow
variables.notes: Follows the GFR decision (0.8 mL/min/kg) at term's renal blood flow / GFR ratio 21 (engine renal rule): ~17. Doppler totals (Visser) are overestimates.

variables.label: Coeliac (liver + spleen) flow
variables.notes: As at 25/28 wk.

variables.label: Ductal shunt flow (L->R)
variables.notes: Small restrictive L->R duct (state).

variables.label: Ductal diameter
variables.notes: State: ~1 mm, restrictive.

variables.label: Foramen ovale shunt (L->R)
variables.notes: Small L->R PFO (state).

variables.label: Respiratory rate
variables.notes: Welty 2018: 29.6 +/- 1.7 wk, 44 h, bubble CPAP 5-8, mostly room air: 67 +/- 20 (direct age); RR falls with maturity; 28 wk 62.

variables.label: Tidal volume
variables.notes: Non-invasive (no mask) convention, caffeine on board.

variables.label: Minute ventilation
variables.notes: RR 60 x Vt 5.0.

variables.label: Inspiratory time fraction (Ti/Ttot)
variables.notes: As at 25/28 wk.

variables.label: Respiratory system compliance
variables.notes: Absolute value at 1.5 kg: lungs 0.9 /kg in series with chest wall 4.5 /kg -> 0.75 /kg.

variables.label: Lung compliance (both lungs)
variables.notes: User decision 0.9: no surfactant, mild RDS in room air on CPAP 5; between acute RDS 0.44 (Bhutani 1988) and recovering 1.0-1.2 (Reiterer, Cunningham); Stoecklin 2024 static CL 0.95 /kg at 36 wk PMA.

variables.label: Chest wall compliance
variables.notes: Stiffens with maturity (Rehan 2001): Gerhardt 6.4 /kg at 32 wk (ventilated), Stoecklin 3.0 at 36 wk PMA; series 7 (25 wk), 5 (28 wk).

variables.label: Respiratory system resistance
variables.notes: Larger airways: 28 wk 65 at 1 kg scaled ~1/weight^0.9 (the 25 -> 28 wk step).

variables.label: Functional residual capacity
variables.notes: CPAP 5: da Silva 1994 22.6 (PEEP 4) - 26.2 (PEEP 5) mL/kg; McEvoy 2002 ~28 at ~32.5 wk; a more compliant lung.

variables.label: Anatomic dead space
variables.notes: Nasopharynx share smaller at larger size (28 wk 3.0, 25 wk 3.2); nCPAP does not wash out the nasopharynx (Liew 2020).

variables.label: Physiological dead space fraction (Vd/Vt)
variables.notes: With MV 300 and VCO2 ~5.7-6.0: VA 120 -> PaCO2 41-43.

variables.label: Inspired O2 fraction
variables.notes: State: nCPAP 5 in room air (user decision); SpO2 is an outcome of the lung, not titrated.

variables.label: Apnoea / periodic breathing
variables.notes: Reference only; Apnea model off at baseline. Less frequent than at 28 wk.

variables.label: SpO2 (pre-ductal)
variables.notes: User decision 96: room air on CPAP 5 with mild RDS. Below the 99.4 % median of distress-free 30-36 wk infants in air (Richard 1993; P5 95.5); above the 90-94 % band used when on oxygen.

variables.label: pH
variables.notes: Derived (Van Slyke) from BE -3 and pCO2 43 (user decision).

variables.label: pCO2
variables.notes: Breathing CO2 check (VA 120, VCO2 5.7-6.0 -> 41-43); PHELBI control band 40-50 on days 1-3.

variables.label: HCO3
variables.notes: Derived from pH and pCO2.

variables.label: Base excess
variables.notes: User decision -3: enteral feeds and a maturer tubule; early metabolic acidosis resolves quickly, base deficit > 10 after day 3 in only 2 % (Senterre 2015). Series -7 (25 wk), -5.5 (28 wk).

variables.label: PaO2
variables.notes: SpO2 96 on the 30 wk curve (P50 19.0 standard, pH 7.33): Severinghaus scaled -> ~64.

variables.label: Hb-O2 P50 (standard)
variables.notes: P50 rises linearly with GA 28-40 wk (Granzotto 1991); <=27 wk 18.5 (De Halleux 2002), term ~19.5-20.

variables.label: Mixed venous O2 saturation
variables.notes: Fick: Hb 15.5, SaO2 0.96 (CaO2 20.1), systemic flow 195, VO2 6.5 -> ~80 %.

variables.label: Oxygen consumption
variables.notes: Caffeine on board and feeds (thermic effect): Kjartansson 1992 6.1 +/- 0.8 (31-36 wk, mean 34, 50 % RH); Bauer 1997 5.8 (<1500 g, week 1); caffeine raises VO2 (Bauer 2001).

variables.label: Respiratory quotient
variables.notes: Milk fat replaces part of the glucose-rich PN (25/28 wk 0.95).

variables.label: Core temperature
variables.notes: Sauer 1984.

variables.label: Incubator relative humidity
variables.notes: Common practice for 28-32 wk in week 1 (series 80 / 70 / 60).

variables.label: Insensible water loss
variables.notes: Skin water loss falls exponentially with GA and with postnatal age (Hammarlund 1982/1983, 28-30 wk group); no numbers in the abstracts. Reference only.

variables.label: Plasma glucose
variables.notes: Advancing feeds, less PN glucose and less insulin resistance than at 25/28 wk (7.0 / 6.5).

variables.label: Lactate
variables.notes: As at 28 wk.

variables.label: Enteral feed volume
variables.notes: State: advancing enteral feeds on day 3 plus PN top-up, 3-hourly boluses. Reference only.

variables.label: Hemoglobin
variables.notes: User decision 15.5. Jopling 2009: birth at 30 wk 16.2 (regression); 29-34 wk shows no early fall; day-3 29-34 wk group Hb ~15.5 (12-20), Hct ~45.

variables.label: Hematocrit
variables.notes: Birth 47.7 % (regression); day-3 29-34 wk group ~45.

variables.label: Fetal haemoglobin fraction
variables.notes: Between <=27 wk 93 % and the falling HbF with GA. Reference only.

variables.label: Blood volume
variables.model_readout: sum of blood compartment volumes / weight
variables.notes: As at 28 wk; delayed clamping.

variables.label: GFR
variables.notes: User decision 0.8 mL/min/kg (0.5-1.1) at BSA 0.129 m2: day 3 = 0.77 x the Vieux 2010 day-7 value 21.7 (the 28 wk ratio). The engine's renal reference rests at the day-7 value (1.08 mL/min/kg), so a GFR factor ~0.77 or acceptance is decided in the first look. Bueva 1994 (31 wk, day 1.5) ~0.5 mL/min/kg.

variables.label: Urine output
variables.notes: Diuretic phase on day 3; water reabsorption ~0.94 at GFR 0.8.

variables.label: Fractional sodium excretion
variables.notes: FENa falls with GA (Gallini 2000); 28 wk 5 %, 25 wk 10 %. Reference only.

variables.label: Plasma creatinine
variables.notes: Bueva 1994: 91 at 31 wk day 1.5; the early rise is smaller at higher GA (Miall 1999). Reference only.
